title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up a general framework for the 'structure at infinity' of moduli spaces M_{g,ν}. The boundary of the Deligne–Mumford compactification is a normal crossings divisor (in the orbifold/stack sense), and its strata are indexed by stable graphs. On the previous page he gave X a 'local stratification structure'. Its strata behave like the leaves of a foliation. Each stratum E has its own topology, not necessarily the induced one, for which E → X is a local immersion. He then defined D*_{Δ0} as the topological sum of all strata, with a canonical map D*_{Δ0} → X that is bijective and a local immersion (296–297).

This page has three remarks on that construction.

(1) Finiteness. If X is compact there are only finitely many strata, and each is locally compact. The text then says roughly: 'one does not introduce here stratifications with infinitely many strata — but of course this finiteness is not stable under passage to an open subset of X.' Restricting to an open set can break a stratum into infinitely many leaves or components.

(2) Localization. The formation of D*_{Δ0} over X commutes with restriction to an open subset U ⊂ X: D*_{Δ0}(U) = D*_{Δ0}(X) ×_X U. This is presumably the reason for using the leaf-wise topology and the sum of strata rather than closed strata.

(3) Consistency with the normal crossings case. Suppose the stratification structure comes from a normal crossings divisor in an analytic space. Let D*_d be the 'open' part of the d-fold locus, i.e. points lying on exactly d local branches, as in the two preceding sections. Then there is a canonical isomorphism (298) D*_{Δ0} ≅ ⨿_{d∈ℕ} D*_d. So the new notation agrees with the old one.

Purpose: this sets up the next page (88). There he introduces flags of strata (diagrams of length ν, Σ_* = {X̄_{i0} ⊂ … ⊂ X̄_{iν}}) with an origin x ∈ X_{i0}, and topologized spaces D*_{Δ_ν} → X. That is a simplicial-type tower generalizing the multiple-point spaces D_d of a normal crossings divisor. It is a precursor of nerve or exit-path constructions for stratified spaces.
errors: In remark (1), 'finitely many strata if X compact' needs a local finiteness hypothesis on the local stratification structure; this is presumably built into the definition.

In remark (3), (298) requires D*_d to mean the locus of exactly d branches, with the leaf topology. With self-crossing components, the strata of D*_{Δ0} are the connected leaves, and their disjoint union recovers ⨿ D*_d. This is fine, but the identification is only stated, not argued.

ideas.what: Space D*_{Δ0} = disjoint sum of strata, each with its own (leaf) topology, mapping bijectively by a local immersion to X; its formation is compatible with restriction to open sets
ideas.modern_name: disjoint union of strata / 'resolution' of a stratified space by its strata; leaf topology as for foliations
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratified-space theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); the leaf-like version echoes foliation theory
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame (modérée) stratified spaces and the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν} only programmatically

ideas.what: For a normal crossings divisor, the sum of strata equals ⨿_d D*_d (open multiple-point loci)
ideas.modern_name: multiple-point strata of an NCD / depth stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Deligne, Hodge II, for the D_d normalizations of multiple-point loci)

ideas.what: Finiteness of strata on compact X and its non-stability under restriction to opens

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine housekeeping remarks (finiteness, compatibility with restriction, consistency with the normal crossings notation) inside Grothendieck's unpublished set-up of a stratified 'structure at infinity'. The more interesting construction, the flag spaces D*_{Δ_ν} akin to exit-path or nerve constructions, begins on the next page, not here.

The crossed words are 'feuilles'/'feuilletages', replaced by 'strates'/'stratifications'.
b) should read: 'La formation de D*_{Δ0} au-dessus de X commute à la restriction à un ouvert de X.'

c) should read: 'Si la structure de strat. est définie par un diviseur à croisements normaux dans un espace analytique, alors on a un isomorphisme (298)...' The crossed word is probably 'structure'/'stratification', not 'fonction'.
